inputs.sbc_source: 10-K/annual report cash flow statements FY2015-FY2025 disclose no stock-based compensation line; SBC-zero market (HK-listed utility, no equity-settled award programme identified). sbc_pct_path held at 0 across all scenarios per house convention (explicit zero row, not omitted).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T08:08:12Z regular HKEX close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 64.30-79.80
inputs.share_count_date: 2025-12-31 (weighted average shares in issue per FY2025 annual report note; unchanged for a decade, no options/SBC dilution)
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD is pegged to USD under the Linked Exchange Rate System (1983-present), so HKD risk-free tracks USD risk-free closely; used as the currency-matched basis per adaptations (a1). CLP is a single-A-rated (S&P A / Moody's A2 CLP Holdings; A+/A1 CLP Power; AA-/A1 CAPCO) regulated utility holdco with ~89% of FY2025 operating earnings before fair value movements and unallocated items from the Hong Kong Scheme of Control (government-guaranteed 8% permitted return on average net fixed assets, 2024-2033 agreement) -- a low-beta, low-cyclicality earnings base. The remaining ~11% (EnergyAustralia merchant generation/retail, Chinese Mainland market-priced renewables, India/Taiwan JV equity income) carries real commodity, FX and competitive risk. Base WACC of 7.0% reflects this blend: closer to the low end used for regulated infrastructure/REIT-like discount rates in this folder than a full cyclical-industrial premium, but above a pure REIT given the ~11-40% (earnings vs revenue view) non-regulated, currency-exposed component. Bear case uses 8.0% (regulatory/merchant risk not fully priced in bear flows also reflected in discount rate is avoided per adaptations (f) -- the +100bp in bear reflects only the genuinely higher cost of capital a stressed, more-merchant-weighted CLP would face, not a duplicate of the flow-level bear assumptions). Bull case uses 6.3% (SoC renewal on favourable terms, full investment-grade access maintained).
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial. Lease liabilities are HK$163m at FY2025 (0.28% of HK$57,901m net debt) -- CLP is capital/transmission-asset heavy, not lease-heavy. No adjustment made to net debt or the flows; the amount is too small to move the valuation under either treatment (A) or (B). Not included in the net_debt figure separately since the filing's own disclosed 'Net debt' already nets it consistently with prior years.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is charged once, folded into a single combined leakage rate applied at the EBIT-to-NOPAT step (cash_tax_rate_path), per adaptations (c) -- the engine's equity bridge only deducts net debt and has no separate NCI deduction, so NCI must be charged in the flows, not the bridge. FY2025 'Profit for the year' (consolidated, before NCI split) was HK$11,546m; attributable to shareholders HK$10,468m; NCI share therefore 9.34%. FY2024 NCI share was 7.7%, FY2023 (loss-affected FY2022 comparative distorts) 13.2%; ~9% is a representative multi-year average. Combined with a ~16.5% HK statutory tax rate (CLP's recent cash tax rate has run 14.5-20.9% of pre-tax profit; 16.5% is the HK profits tax statutory rate and a reasonable normalized cash rate), the combined EBIT-to-NOPAT leakage is 1-(1-0.165)*(1-0.09) = ~24.0%, used as cash_tax_rate_path. This is NOT a pure tax rate -- it is tax-plus-NCI-leakage by construction, and the label is kept as cash_tax_rate_path only because that is the engine's only EBIT-to-NOPAT driver. Calibration check: HK$14,272m FY2025 EBIT proxy (EBITDA 23,990 - D&A 9,718) x (1-0.24) = HK$10,847m modelled NOPAT vs HK$10,468m actual attributable net income -- within ~3.6%, the residual being net interest expense and other items the unlevered EBIT proxy does not capture (expected, since the engine discounts unlevered flows and net interest is priced via WACC and the net-debt deduction, not as a flow-level charge).
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: Owner-FCF DCF (component route) with non-US/cyclical adaptations per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/references/owner-fcf-adaptations.md, NOT a REIT/AFFO or bank/residual-income model. CLP is a regulated-return utility holdco (HK Scheme of Control: government-guaranteed 8% permitted return on average net fixed assets, 2024-2033), but unlike a REIT its reported net income is not dominated by fair-value/revaluation noise, it generates real (mostly positive) free cash flow across the historical decade, and total_debt/net_debt behave as genuine financial leverage (not deposits or AFFO-embedded financing). The regulated character is instead captured INSIDE the owner-FCF engine via conservative growth (capped near RAB-growth-plus-demand-growth rates, not open-ended), stable margins (no assumed re-rating), and an elevated near-term capex path (2024-2028 HK$52.9bn Development Plan funds RAB growth, so capex/revenue is well above D&A/revenue in the near term and tapers as the plan completes) -- directly analogous to AIA.NZ's 'capex supercycle -> component owner-FCF+taper' treatment noted in memory for a comparable infrastructure name. Net debt used is the company's own disclosed 'Net debt' figure (HK$57,901m per the FY2025 annual report net-debt-to-total-capital note), which is closely consistent with total_debt (61,829) less cash (3,905) = 57,924 -- the small gap is other financial assets netted in the company's own definition; the disclosed figure is used as the more precise anchor. Interest income (HK$194m FY2025) is NOT stripped from FCF: CLP is a net DEBTOR (net debt ~HK$58bn, far exceeding cash of HK$3.9bn), so the interest-income-double-count rule (which applies only when net cash exceeds ~1x the FCF base) does not apply here -- net interest EXPENSE is already correctly embedded in reported OCF and is not separately adjusted, consistent with an unlevered-FCF-then-subtract-net-debt DCF. SBC is genuinely zero (no stock-based compensation disclosed in any of 11 years of filings) -- house and street bases coincide; band_position is reported as null per adaptations (e). Shares outstanding held flat at the weighted-average 2,526.451m for a decade with zero issuance and zero buybacks (DividendsPaid is the sole capital-return channel; ShareRepurchases is 0 in every year) -- annual_share_growth_pct = 0.0 is both the SBC convention AND the observed reality here, a rare case where the two coincide exactly. FY2022 (near-zero net income of HK$924m, EBITDA margin collapsed to 9.8%) was a fuel-cost/hedging shock (global energy crisis following Russia's invasion of Ukraine) -- a genuine one-off, excluded from consideration as a representative base year and flagged as the reason the 3-year net income CAGR (124%, an artifact of the FY2022 trough denominator) is not used as the growth anchor. Revenue and equity CAGRs cluster tightly (10yr revenue CAGR 0.87%, 10yr equity CAGR 1.46%, 5yr revenue CAGR 2.03%) -- consistent with a mature regulated utility and well within the 30% divergence flag threshold; equity CAGR (the house default) is used as the terminal-growth anchor, projected forward growth in early years is set modestly above this trailing average to reflect disclosed near-term demand tailwinds (data centre electricity sales +7.5% FY2025, +11.8% H1 2026; Northern Metropolis buildout) that are not fully visible in the trailing decade's blended growth.

historical_growth.notes: FCF and EPS multi-year CAGRs are not computable (FY2022 FCF was negative, -HK$1,819m, and FY2022 EPS collapsed to HK$0.37 -- a fuel-cost/hedging shock, not a trend). Revenue and equity CAGRs cluster in the 0.9-2.0% range across the 5yr and 10yr windows and do not diverge >30% from each other -- no divergence flag warranted. The 3yr revenue CAGR (-4.38%) and 3yr equity CAGR (0.66%) both reflect FY2022's elevated revenue (fuel cost pass-through inflated the top line even as margins collapsed) as the start-point; not used as the primary anchor for the same reason. selected_growth_rate (1.46%, equity 10yr) is used as the terminal-growth anchor; explicit-year growth is set modestly higher near-term per the disclosed data centre/Northern Metropolis demand tailwind, tapering to this level by the outer projection years.

base.narrative: The Hong Kong Scheme of Control continues to deliver its guaranteed 8% permitted return on a steadily growing regulated asset base through the current 2024-2028 Development Plan (HK$52.9bn) and beyond, funded by data centre connections (+7.5% FY2025, +11.8% H1 2026), Northern Metropolis buildout and transport electrification. EnergyAustralia stabilises after FY2025's retail-margin trough as 2026 AEMC reforms settle and the flexible-capacity pipeline (Wooreen, Orana, Kidston, Hallett) comes online ahead of Yallourn's 2028 retirement. Chinese Mainland renewables growth continues but at a more disciplined, lower-multiple pace as CLP prioritises returns over volume amid the shift to market-based pricing. Capex remains elevated near-term to fund the RAB, then tapers toward a maintenance-plus-growth level as the current Development Plan cycle completes around FY2028-2029, allowing free cash flow to recover. NCI leakage (~9%, mostly India/Apraava and Mainland JV structures) and a ~16.5% HK statutory tax rate are the two structural drags on unlevered flows reaching shareholders.

bull.narrative: SoC renewal terms remain favourable well beyond 2033 and the permitted-return framework is not tightened despite tariff-affordability pressure. Data centre and Northern Metropolis demand exceeds current guidance, accelerating growth in the SoC-regulated asset base. EnergyAustralia's flexible-capacity buildout (BESS, pumped hydro) captures outsized returns from rising wholesale price volatility as coal retires faster than replacement capacity, reversing FY2025's retail-margin collapse. Apraava Energy's 100%-non-carbon India portfolio and selective, higher-return Mainland renewables investment lift JV/associate equity income meaningfully. Credit ratings and green/Panda bond access keep funding costs low through the capex programme, and growth capex normalizes faster than base case as projects complete on schedule.

bear.narrative: A future SoC review reduces the permitted return below 8% or tightens capex pass-through as Hong Kong tariff-affordability pressure intensifies, compressing the earnings base that funds ~89% of Group operating earnings. EnergyAustralia's retail margin pressure persists through the 2026 AEMC reforms (price caps, disclosure mandates) and the proposed free-midday-electricity policy, with customer churn continuing. Chinese Mainland curtailment keeps rising past the 15% (H1 2026) level as market-based pricing displaces fixed benchmark tariffs faster than CLP can reallocate capital to higher-return projects, and India/Apraava JV governance friction with CDPQ limits capital redeployment. Yallourn closure costs and mine rehabilitation run above the HK$345m FY2025 provision. Net debt keeps rising (already HK$57.9bn to HK$62.2bn in H1 2026 alone) faster than earnings, tightening headroom under the A-range credit ratings and raising funding costs into a higher-for-longer rate environment, which is reflected in the higher bear WACC (genuinely higher cost of capital for a more merchant-weighted, more levered CLP, not a duplicate of the flow-level risk).

scenario_narratives.base: Hong Kong SoC delivers its guaranteed 8% return on a steadily growing RAB through the 2024-2028 Development Plan and beyond; EnergyAustralia stabilises post-FY2025 trough; Mainland growth continues at a disciplined pace; capex tapers as the current plan cycle completes.
scenario_narratives.bull: SoC renewal stays favourable past 2033, HK demand (data centres, Northern Metropolis) exceeds guidance, EnergyAustralia's flexible-capacity bets pay off as volatility rises, and Apraava/Mainland JV equity income scales faster on selective high-return investment.
scenario_narratives.bear: A future SoC review compresses the permitted return or tightens capex pass-through, EnergyAustralia's margin pressure persists through 2026 reforms, Mainland curtailment keeps rising, Yallourn costs overrun, and rising net debt tightens credit headroom.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight held above the house default 15% (raised to 25%) because CLP carries genuine regulatory concentration risk (a single regulator/franchise, the HK SoC, funds ~89% of operating earnings, and the current agreement is not reviewed again until closer to its December 2033 expiry but is 'subject to periodic government reviews' per the company's own risk disclosure) stacked on top of a genuinely volatile, currently-underperforming merchant segment (EnergyAustralia operating earnings fell 85.6% in FY2025). Bull weight trimmed to 25% (from the 35% default) because the bull case requires several partly-independent things to go right simultaneously (favourable SoC renewal economics, an EnergyAustralia turnaround, AND accelerating high-return Mainland/India growth) rather than one dominant lever. Base case takes the balance at 50%, reflecting that the SoC framework's remaining seven years to 2033 provide a high-confidence floor under the dominant earnings stream even if the merchant pieces underperform.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CLP Holdings is valued as a regulated-return utility holdco via the owner-FCF component DCF (not AFFO/REIT or bank residual-income, since net income here is a real, not fair-value-noise-dominated, earnings figure and the company generates genuine free cash flow). The regulated character (HK Scheme of Control, ~89% of FY2025 operating earnings, guaranteed 8% return on a RAB that grows through the disclosed 2024-2028 Development Plan) is captured through capped, RAB-linked growth rather than open-ended extrapolation, stable margins with no assumed re-rating, and an explicit near-term capex supercycle (capex running 1.5-1.6x D&A on revenue) that tapers toward a maintenance-plus-growth level once the current plan cycle completes -- the same treatment applied to AIA.NZ's comparable capex-supercycle infrastructure profile. A ~24% combined tax-plus-NCI leakage rate (statutory ~16.5% HK tax blended with a calibrated ~9% NCI share of consolidated profit) is charged once at the EBIT-to-NOPAT step, since NCI has no separate deduction elsewhere in the model. SBC is genuinely zero across the entire eleven-year filing history -- house and street bases coincide by construction. WACC (7.0% base) reflects the HKD/USD currency peg (HKD risk-free tracks USD closely) and CLP's single-A credit ratings, set below a typical cyclical-industrial rate to reflect the SoC's low-beta earnings floor, but above a pure REIT/AFFO rate given the real commodity, FX and competitive risk carried by the ~11% (earnings-mix view) merchant/JV segments.
key_risks_to_valuation: Scheme of Control renewal/renegotiation risk beyond December 2033, or an interim tightening of the permitted-return framework or capex-approval process under tariff-affordability pressure

EnergyAustralia retail margin structurally impaired by 2026 AEMC reforms (price caps, disclosure mandates) and a proposed federal free-midday-electricity policy, on top of already-intense competition and customer churn

Chinese Mainland shift to market-based renewable pricing (all new projects since June 2025) combined with rising curtailment (15% in H1 2026 vs 9% a year earlier) making Mainland growth capital less productive than modelled
Currency translation risk across AUD, RMB and INR flattering or depressing reported HKD results independent of underlying operating performance
Rising net debt (HK$57.9bn to HK$62.2bn in H1 2026 alone) funding a large multi-market capex programme, at a time of coal-transition costs (Yallourn 2028 closure) and safety/reputational incidents
India/Apraava Energy 50:50 JV governance with CDPQ limiting CLP's unilateral control over capital allocation and the pace of the now-fully-non-carbon portfolio's growth
